newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Sterling rally unabated, more rate hikes seen.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Sterling rally unabated, more rate hikes seen.

text.p: Sterling bulls were undeterred on Thursday by a rise of just 1/4 point in Bank of England interest rates, and appeared determined to drive the pound higher on the prospect of more monetary tightening to come.
The British stock market breathed a sigh of relief, hoping that the 1/4 point increase would not halt the consumer boom which has been pumping cash into a buoyant retail sector.
Sterling initially dropped on the news base rates had been increased to 6.75 percent on disappointment that the Bank had not provided a more aggressive 1/2 point hike.
But investors on the foreign exchange market quickly reassessed the outlook for interest rates and saw the cost of credit moving yet higher.

"Nothing has happened that could take the shine off sterling," said David Bloom, currency strategist at HSBC James Capel. "It will continue to be driven higher by favourable interest rate differentials."
Sterling fluctuated wildly after the news, first falling about a pfennig to around 2.9550 marks, then recovering above 2.9600 before easing yet again back to 2.9550 at 1240 GMT.

However, the upward drive was expected to continue as economists predicted further rate rises. "The positive backdrop to the pound should be sustained," said Jeremy Hawkins, chief economist at Bank of America.
Following last week's budget, the pound set a six-year high of 2.9760 marks.
The budget, the first from a Labour government in nearly two decades, was widely interpreted as putting the burden of slowing down strong consumer demand on monetary policy.
On the stock market, the FTSE 100 index of blue chip shares partially recovered earlier losses on the news of the rate rise.
In early afternoon trading the FTSE was hovering around 4,756, down six from the previous close but well off the day's low of 4,732.7
Share market analysts also thought there may well be more monetary tightening further down the road.
But there was relief that the Bank of England had held back at least for now.

An immediate 1/2 point hammer blow from the monetary policy committee could have sent sterling shooting up even more strongly, putting further pressure on exporters already reeling from an 18 percent rise in the pound in just under one year.
"They (the exporters) were so bombed out anyway that it was guaranteed that something like this would make people look at them again," said one trader.
Retailers benefited most, with stores group Kingfisher leading the rally.
At one stage Kingfisher were up nearly seven percent at 739, before they settled back to 717-1/2 for a rise of 25 pence on the day.
Electrical retailer Dixons, already on a roll on the back of strong trading figures out on Wednesday, put on another 25 pence to trade at 561-1/2.

On the government bond market there was a mixed reaction. The September gilts future initially jumped on relief that the Bank of England had only raised moderately. But that market fell back later on prospects of further rate rises.
"It is going to leave the idea that there is another rate rise to come and probably next month," said one trader.
An hour after the rate rise the the September contract was unchanged from its previous close at 114-09/32.
